PSALM 83

. Of Asaph--(See on , title). The historical occasion is probably that of , (compare ; ). After a general petition, the craft and rage of the combined enemies are described, God's former dealings recited, and a like summary and speedy destruction on them is invoked.

1. God addressed as indifferent (compare ; ).

be not still--literally, "not quiet," as opposed to action.
2. thine enemies--as well as ours (; Is 37:23).
3. hidden ones--whom God specially protects (; ).

4. from being a nation--utter destruction (; ).

Israel--here used for Judah, having been the common name.

5. they have consulted--with heart, or cordially.

together--all alike.

6-8. tabernacles--for people ().

they--all these united with the children of Lot, or Ammonites and Moabites (compare ).
9-11. Compare the similar fate of these () with that of the foes mentioned in , here referred to. They destroyed one another (; ). Human remains form manure (compare ; ).

12. The language of the invaders.

houses--literally, "residences," enclosures, as for flocks ().

of God--as the proprietors of the land (; ).
13. like a wheel--or, whirling of any light thing (), as stubble or chaff ().
14-15. Pursue them to an utter destruction.

16. that they may seek--or as , supply "men," since , 18 amplify the sentiment of , expressing more fully the measure of destruction, and the lesson of God's being and perfections (compare ) taught to all men.
